Placide Cappeau wrote the French words in December 1847, on a stagecoach from Macon to Dijon, for Midnight Mass in Roquemaure. Adolphe Adam set them within days, and it was first sung there that Christmas.

John Sullivan Dwight, the American critic and minister who wrote the English words in 1855, was an abolitionist, and admired the song's stress on human equality.
